PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-10-07
47F, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. She reports feeling well overall and takes her blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. She works as an accountant, mostly seated, and walks most evenings. Mother with breast cancer. Father with heart failure. Appetite is good, weight stable, and sleep is about 7 hours most nights. She has good support at home and asks about screening she is due for. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 122/76, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 158 lb, BMI 26.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 5.5%.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 120/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Family history: discussed relevant family history and reviewed warning signs to report, such as new breathlessness, swelling in the legs, or reduced exercise tolerance. Confirmed mammography is up to date.
3. Health maintenance: cervical screening up to date; colorectal screening discussed for her age. Influenza vaccine given today. Encouraged continued evening walks and light strength work.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
